prompt: A photorealistic product-photography presentation sheet showing SIX separate everyday desk objects arranged in a perfectly even grid of 3 columns and 2 rows: the empty-state visuals of a calm, premium banking app, in the style of the modern realistic object visuals of Revolut and Qonto. Background: one seamless pure white #FFFFFF studio sweep, completely flat, no horizon line, no vignette, no gradient, no visible table edge. Every object stands alone in its own invisible cell, centred, all six at the same scale and the same visual size (each about 60 percent of its cell width and height), all standing on the same invisible floor line within their row, with clear empty white space between them so that no two objects or shadows touch. One photographed set with identical treatment: All six photographed from exactly the same camera position: straight from the front at eye level, the camera level with the middle of the objects, looking straight at their front faces. Every object faces the viewer, turned at most 10 to 15 degrees to the left so that its depth and side edge still read as a real three-dimensional object. A moderate telephoto lens with no wide-angle distortion. NOT a top-down view, NOT an isometric view, NOT seen from above, NOT lying flat. The same soft but directional studio light from one large softbox at the upper left, giving gentle tonal gradients across every surface and subtle ambient occlusion in the folds, and the same soft natural contact shadow on the invisible white floor directly beneath each object, fading out towards the lower right, like a high-end product photograph, not a flat 3D render. Real materials rendered with true physical detail: thick uncoated cotton paper with a visible fine fibre and slightly soft edges, matte bead-blasted aluminium, matte soft-touch lacquer, smooth heavy coloured board. Restrained palette only: deep ink-blue #17284A (a clear dark blue navy, not purple, not black), clean cool paper white, pale blue-grey #D6E0F0, satin silver, and fountain-pen blue #2546A6 used only for the few ink marks. Top row, left: an envelope of heavy deep ink-blue paper standing upright on its long bottom edge and facing the viewer, its flap folded open upwards behind it, with a folded sheet of white cotton letter paper standing up out of it, so that the upper half of the blank white letter clearly rises above the envelope. Top row, middle: a single sheet of thick white cotton paper in portrait orientation standing upright and facing the viewer, very slightly curved so that it stands on its own; on it only a few very faint pale blue-grey bars where the lines of a form would be, and near its bottom right one single short gentle wave line of fountain-pen-blue ink, one smooth curve that is clearly not a letter; in front of the paper a closed matte ink-blue fountain pen with a satin silver clip lies on the floor, parallel to the bottom edge of the sheet. Top row, right: a slim matte silver aluminium laptop, open, seen from the front with its screen facing the viewer straight on, the keyboard deck visible only as a thin foreshortened strip below the screen; the screen glows softly with an abstract video-call layout: a pale blue-grey background, one large rounded rectangle tile in a soft blue gradient and a short row of three small round buttons below it; no person, no face, no text on the screen. Bottom row, left: a closed document folder of smooth deep ink-blue board standing upright on its bottom edge and facing the viewer, with the top edges of three or four white paper sheets clearly sticking out of its top, slightly fanned, and one pale blue-grey elastic band running vertically around it. Bottom row, middle: a small standing easel desk calendar facing the viewer straight on, with a white wire binding along the top; its front page is white paper with a clean grid of empty squares drawn in faint pale blue-grey lines, and one single square near the lower right is filled solid ink-blue; absolutely no numbers, no month name, no letters. Bottom row, right: a small white paper card standing upright and facing the viewer, with one round ink-blue rubber-stamp impression on its right half showing only a bold check mark inside a clean double ring (no words in the stamp); in front of the card, slightly to the left so that the impression stays fully visible, a compact matte ink-blue desk stamp standing upright on the floor. Strictly no text, no letters, no numbers, no digits, no readable writing, no logos or brand marks, no people, no faces, no hands. No glossy plastic, no cartoon proportions, no toy-like look, no clay render, no isometric view, no top-down view, no outlines, no neon, no glow, no sparkles, no bright saturated colours, no colours other than the listed palette.
